title: Pluggable SDK Error Adapters + Runtime Diagnostic Hints
creator: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: SDKs currently expose surface-level exceptions with inconsistent codes and sparse runtime diagnostic context. That makes it hard for customers and SREs to: (1) decide safe retry boundaries for transient failures, (2) offer precise remediation instructions to end users, and (3) correlate client-side errors to server-side incidents. Goal: implement a pluggable "error adapter" interface in each SDK (Python/TS/Go) that normalizes server/network/runtime errors into a canonical classification and attaches a small, machine-readable diagnostic envelope to every error instance. The envelope is designed to be safe for logs and support quick triage: request_id, model_variant, backend_region, kernel_path_hint, kv_cache_hit (yes/no), estimated_lat_ms, token_index (if streaming), attempted_retries, and a short human_actionable_hint. Non-goal: changing existing server error codes or replacing runtime telemetry—this ticket focuses on SDK surface, mapping heuristics, and ergonomics/examples.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a documented ErrorAdapter interface that teams can implement or opt into via factory registration
Default adapters for Python, TS, and Go classify errors into: transient_retryable, throttled_backoff, auth_failure, client_validation, and fatal_server_error
Errors include a textual actionable hint (one sentence) and a diagnostic envelope with the agreed fields
Streaming errors (partial responses) include token_index or last_chunk_marker and explicit resume guidance where possible
Library tests cover mapping heuristics and include a small curated dataset of 40 representative server error payloads
Documentation pages with migration guide and language-specific examples (retry loops with backoff, how to inspect envelope) are published
E2E: when a simulated transient backend error is thrown, the SDK auto-classifies and a sample_retry_policy in docs demonstrates safe retry sequence
implementation_notes: Design a minimal cross-language envelope schema as a flat key set: [request_id, model_variant, backend_region, kernel_path_hint, kv_cache_hit, estimated_lat_ms, token_index, attempted_retries, hint]
Expose the envelope on error objects as .diagnostics (Python), .diagnostics (TS), Diagnostics() method (Go) — keep naming consistent across languages
ErrorAdapter responsibilities: parse server payload, enrich with client-side context (latency, retries), classify category, emit hint message
Default adapters are conservative: prefer false negatives for retryable classification rather than spurious retries that change downstream state
Provide helper primitives: RetryDecision enum, isRetryable(error) predicate, suggestedBackoff(error) returning milliseconds
Add small conversion layer so SDKs can accept server-side structured error payloads and also raw 5xx/timeout network errors
Streaming clients attach last_received_token_index and include a resume_hint when the server returns a resumable cursor
risks: Over-enriching the envelope could expose sensitive data—we restrict fields to IDs and telemetry, avoid user content
Inconsistent names across languages could harm cross-team debugging: enforce a single agreed spec and tests
Default classification heuristics might be incorrect for some custom customer deployments (edge proxies) — must provide easy opt-out/custom adapter
Keeping the envelope small to avoid log volume and PII leakage may limit future debugging needs; add a gated opt-in verbose mode
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter parsing with synthetic server error payloads (40 cases covering 400/401/429/500/503, timeouts, connection reset, malformed JSON)
Property tests for isRetryable across combinations of status code, error_code string, and header hints (x-retry-after)
Integration test that spins up a test harness that returns resumable-stream failures and asserts streaming client includes resume_hint and token_index
Fuzz test for malformed diagnostics and large headers to ensure envelope truncation behaves as expected
Manual verification: run sample app in Docker that logs error.diagnostics for Python/TS/Go and inspect parity across SDKs
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the diagnostic envelope in each SDK (off by default). Release behind minor versions sdks-2026.04-py, sdks-2026.04-ts, sdks-2026.04-go
Roll out default adapter enabled for internal dogfood customers and Redwood-managed Dedicated customers first
Collect anonymous telemetry (opt-in) on classification accuracy for two weeks, then enable broadly if no regressions
Publish migration doc with examples and explain how to implement custom adapters to preserve existing behavior
Coordinate with runtime team to add a stable server-side structured error shape in a follow-up ticket (link in dependencies)
